prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to destroy chosen proteins

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep targeted protein degradation as my single preferred part. It is the one candidate whose concept is new in kind: event-driven pharmacology in which a designed molecule brings an E3 ligase and a target together, so that the target is removed instead of occupied. Crews and Deshaies proposed and demonstrated this in 2001. Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explained an entire drug class and showed that the same logic works through glues, with the mechanism confirmed independently in many laboratories. The chair's summary shows that all eight members place B026 in their round-1 files, six of them as an alternative or preferred part, and nobody disputes the science or the independent confirmation. The remaining objections concern timing and allocation, and I think both can be answered in the citation. A citation that speaks of directing the ubiquitin-proteasome system, and not of PROTACs alone, covers the heterobifunctional and the glue strand together without naming eight people.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC drug is approved, so the clinical proof lags behind the mechanistic proof, and five members regard recognition as early. The three-name cap leaves out Ciulli, Gray, Ito, Kim and Sakamoto, each of whom made decisive contributions, and a trio of Crews, Deshaies and Handa spans two strands that some members see as two discoveries. If the committee will not accept that, B065 is the most cleanly attributable alternative and I would vote for it rather than see the prize stall. I also grant that a protein degradation prize leaves the committee open to the criticism that the field is still being defined.

responses.point: Argues that C-N coupling is novel through ligand-controlled mechanism (amide-bound palladium, difficult reductive elimination) and that three members share an identical two-name allocation.
responses.response: The mechanistic argument is stronger than I credited in round 1: forcing reductive elimination from an amido-palladium intermediate is a real physical-organic problem and not simply the 2010 reaction with nitrogen substituted for carbon. That moves B065 from a safe alternative to a prize I could support on its merits. My remaining difference is about type of advance. Buchwald and Hartwig matured a recognised catalytic strategy, whereas degradation creates a mode of drug action that did not exist before 2001. Your point that Kosugi is a priority question is also fair, and I would handle it in the citation wording because including him would breach the two-name core that makes B065 attractive.

responses.point: Prefers Ciulli as third laureate on B026 because his structure-guided VHL ligands made PROTAC design rational, and notes that the glue strand is a distinct sub-discovery.
responses.response: We still agree on the science, and I take your argument about Ciulli seriously: ternary-complex structures and the VHL ligand are what turned the concept into a design discipline. I stay with Handa because the cereblon finding is the only part of the field with a decades-old drug class behind it, and it is what the citation needs in order not to be a PROTAC-only prize that leaves out the glue strand you yourself call a distinct sub-discovery. The difference between us is one name and I would not block a configuration with Ciulli if that is what secures a majority. I would rather lose Handa than lose the field.

responses.point: Narrowed B037 to Balasubramanian and Klenerman and argues that sequencing by synthesis with reversible terminators is chemistry in its core, with no maturity question.
responses.response: The narrowing to the Solexa pair is a real improvement and answers the Mayer, Rothberg and Ju problem better than your opening trio did. The reversible-terminator chemistry and surface cluster readout are chemistry. What I cannot get past is that the downstream impact is genomics, and the 1980 sequencing prize makes a second sequencing prize in chemistry harder to defend as a new principle. I therefore leave B037 outside my configuration, though a pair this clean is better than the multi-name allocations elsewhere.

responses.point: Keeps B045 first, arguing that lipid phase behaviour, pH-dependent charge and nonbilayer structure are the chemistry behind nucleic-acid delivery, and that the carrier is the part of the mRNA story the 2023 Medicine prize did not recognise.
responses.response: That is the best answer to my own round-1 worry that B045 reads as pharmaceutics. The ionizable-lipid design logic is physical chemistry and the 2023 prize did not honour the carrier. My difficulty remains credit: the Vancouver trio, the Anderson and Langer lipidoid line and MacLachlan are all defensible, and I do not see how the record settles that this year. I therefore keep B045 as an alternative, and I would support it more readily than B056 or B037 if degradation and C-N coupling both stall.

responses.point: Describes C-N coupling as a completely matured reaction class that is the kind of achievement the chemistry prize exists to reward, and asks whether Kosugi and Migita should be credited.
responses.response: As someone who does not work in synthetic methodology, I take your judgment that scope and predictability changed route planning very seriously, and the maturity argument is not in doubt. Our disagreement is whether a second cross-coupling prize within sixteen years is the best use of the slot while a new modality remains unrecognised. On Kosugi and Migita I agree with you and Chabes that the clean pair is worth keeping, with the tin-amide precedent acknowledged in the citation wording.

uncertainties: Whether five members can accept a prize in targeted protein degradation before the first approved PROTAC drug.
Whether the trio of Crews, Deshaies and Handa will be accepted as one achievement, or whether Ciulli should replace Handa to secure a majority.
Whether B065 is judged novel enough after the 2010 prize, since it is the configuration with the most explicit support and may be the realistic majority option.
Whether the committee prefers a mature, cleanly attributed prize to an earlier one in a still-evolving field.
statement.conflict_note: No change. Xiaodong Zou is a Stockholm University colleague, but she prefers B056 and neither my preferred part nor my alternatives involve her work, so I see no conflict requiring recusal. As Secretary and a member since 2015, shared with Johan Aqvist, I have no candidate-specific tie to any name on the shortlist.
